opti-1: Night on a Florida beach. Something big crawls out of the sea.
opti-2: A loggerhead sea turtle lays about 100 eggs, then heads back to sea.
opti-3: For about two months, the warm sand keeps the eggs cozy.
opti-5: The sand's temperature decides if the hatchlings are boys or girls.
opti-6: So scientists measure. They take temperatures and weigh hatchlings.
opti-7: Measuring tells us what our eyes can't.
opti-8: How can you measure and compare the properties of different objects?
26-02-welcome: Our film starts on a Florida beach at night, where scientists guard a nest. First, inspect an old machine with two bowls.
26-02-lesson: Today you're a field scientist. Follow a turtle nest, test two balls, then climb a temperature ladder.
26-02-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
26-02-assign: Time to show what you learned. Build a bar graph, then tell us why tools beat guessing.
how-26-02-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the machine, then tap 3 things you notice.
how-26-02-compare: Put the ruler under one tray and the balance under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Run the test. Then swap.
how-26-02-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing step: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the photo shows.
how-26-02-det: Pick three files, one at a time. Tap a clue, then name the property being measured. Predict the tool, and watch it at work.
how-26-02-partc: Draw a bar graph of the four hatchling masses from Part A. Label the bottom with A, B, C, and D, and the side with grams. Give your graph a title.
